subject.title: fix(agents): avoid symlink-follow in auth.json bootstrap

question: Should exact no-follow-safe mode preservation for rename and copy fallback live in `@openclaw/fs-safe`, or may this PR keep the hardening in OpenClaw's shared wrapper?
rationale: The remaining blocker is a security-sensitive dependency and plugin-facing compatibility boundary, not the direct auth bootstrap fix itself.

options.title: Move exact-mode hardening into fs-safe
options.body: Patch or update `@openclaw/fs-safe` so both rename and copy fallback preserve exact modes without final-path chmod, then keep OpenClaw's wrapper thin.

options.title: Approve a wrapper-level repair
options.body: Keep the OpenClaw wrapper boundary but require copy-fallback mode preservation tests and implementation before merge.

options.title: Narrow this PR to auth bootstrap
options.body: Land only the `auth.json` bootstrap change and track shared atomic replacement chmod hardening separately.

recommendation.title: Move exact-mode hardening into fs-safe
recommendation.body: Patch or update `@openclaw/fs-safe` so both rename and copy fallback preserve exact modes without final-path chmod, then keep OpenClaw's wrapper thin.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans agents auth and the secops-owned file-permission boundary documented for this path.
